title: A nonempty affine open factor of a split Galois fibre has a rational point
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme and $Z\to Y$ a finite etale $G$-torsor for a finite group $G$ [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $F$ be a field, $s:\operatorname{Spec}F\to Y$, and $z:\operatorname{Spec}F\to Z$ with $\pi z=s$. Let $K$ be a field and $b:\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}F$. Let $A$ be a nonzero commutative $K$-algebra and $g:\operatorname{Spec}A\to Z\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}K$ an open immersion, with base change along $sb$ [def-pc-fibre-product], whose composite with the projection to $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is the canonical structural morphism. Then there exists a $K$-algebra homomorphism $A\to K$.

source.place: Tag 0EYI(2) and the torsor splitting used in 0EYJ

proof.text: Let r=bz. Pair the map from Spec A to Z with its structural morphism followed by r, obtaining chi:Spec A to Z times_Y Z. Compose chi with the inverse of the torsor isomorphism coproduct_G Z to Z times_Y Z. Choose a point x of Spec A, which exists since A is nonzero, and a coproduct component containing its image. On the open inverse image V of that component, lift to a map k:V to Z. The two projections of the torsor identity say that g on V is the structural map of V followed by the K-valued translate r_m of r.

At x this equality puts the image point of r_m in the image of g. Spec K has just one point, so the entire image of r_m is contained in the image of g. The universal lifting property of an open immersion gives a:Spec K to Spec A with ag=r_m. The given structural-map identity and the second pullback projection show that a is over Spec K. Full faithfulness of Spec then gives a ring map A to K that commutes with the K-algebra maps. This is the required K-algebra homomorphism.

mathlib_searches.query: A finite Galois torsor with a rational point is trivial and every nonempty open factor has a rational point
A finite etale torsor over a field with a rational point is split and every nonempty open subscheme has a rational point
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits on etale algebras over fields and etale loci, including Algebra.Etale.iff_exists_algEquiv_prod. None uses a rational torsor point to prove rational points on open factors.
mathlib_searches.verdict: No matching theorem; the statement is proved directly from the torsor identity.

mathlib_searches.query: tame|normalization.*chart|GaloisCover.*rational|GaloisCover.*split; rg in Mathlib, WeilConjectures and Sheaf
mathlib_searches.results: Direct rg in WeilConjectures found EtaleTorsor.bijective_smulHom and its local coproduct-lifting proof, which is specific to additive torsors and maps in the small etale site. No corresponding theorem for arbitrary finite groups and affine open factors. Mathlib supplies sigmaOpenCover, IsOpenImmersion.lift and Spec full faithfulness.
mathlib_searches.verdict: No duplicate; reuse the categorical local-lifting argument and Mathlib primitives.

lean.statement:
theorem GaloisCover.open_factor_rational_point
    {Y : Scheme.{u}} (G : Type (u + 1)) [Group G] [Finite G]
    (Z : GaloisCover G Y) (F : CommRingCat.{u}) [Field F]
    (s : Spec F ⟶ Y)
    (hZ : ∃ z : Spec F ⟶ Z.P, z ≫ Z.π = s)
    (K : Type u) [Field K]
    (b : Spec (CommRingCat.of K) ⟶ Spec F)
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra K A] [Nontrivial A]
    (g : Spec (CommRingCat.of A) ⟶ pullback Z.π (b ≫ s))
    (hg : IsOpenImmersion g)
    (hw : g ≫ pullback.snd Z.π (b ≫ s) =
      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K A))) :
    Nonempty (A →ₐ[K] K)
